| [NOTE-760](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-760.md) | Grünwald & Roos — Minimum Description Length Revisited | A review of MDL since 2007. Each model is replaced by one universal distribution, chosen for small worst-case log-loss regret against the model's best fit. NML is the minimax choice, with complexity (k/2) log(n/2π) + log ∫ v√\|I\| + o(1). Estimation is penalised ML with a luckiness function v. | [NOTE-801](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-801.md) | Vitányi & Li — MDL induction, Bayesianism and Kolmogorov complexity | With the universal prior, the Fundamental Inequality puts −log Pr(D\|H) − log P(H) within α = K(Pr(·\|H)) + K(P) of K(D\|H) + K(H) when D is random for H and H is random for P. So ideal MDL and MAP agree to a factor 2^{−α} among such "admissible" hypotheses. α can be as large as K(H), and outside the admissible set the two can pick different hypotheses. For finite-set models, MAP, ideal MDL and Kolmogorov's minimal sufficient statistic coincide. | Read |
| [NOTE-1481](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-1481.md) | LaMont & Wiggins — thermodynamics and inference | Takes the evidence as a partition function with sample size N as inverse temperature, and reads off the thermodynamic derivatives. The internal energy is the leave-one-out predictive loss; the heat capacity becomes a "learning capacity" equal to K/2 in a regular model (equipartition) and to Watanabe's learning coefficient in a singular one, and smaller when prior or discreteness fixes parameters ("freeze-out"). A prior making the Gibbs entropy zero reproduces AIC. The correspondence is formal; nothing in it is a physical current or dissipation. | Read |

| [NOTE-2240](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2240.md) | Transtrum, Machta & Sethna 2010 — why nonlinear fits are hard: the hyper-ribbon and geodesic acceleration | A four-page letter casting least-squares fitting as geometry: the model manifold in data space, with metric JᵀJ, is typically bounded and ribbon-like, its widths falling by a roughly constant factor, which the authors explain by polynomial interpolation for analytic models of one variable; in one eight-parameter model the widths along the metric's eigendirections track √λ over four decades. | [NOTE-2242](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2242.md) | Transtrum, Machta, Brown, Daniels, Myers & Sethna 2015 — sloppiness, the hyperribbon and emergent theories | A Perspective on the Sethna group's programme. Sloppiness is Fisher eigenvalues "roughly evenly spaced in log-space", with no well-defined boundary between stiff and sloppy; because eigenvalues are not invariant, the invariant content is the bounded model manifold with exponentially falling widths, the hyperribbon, for which √λ in dimensionless parameters is "a reliable approximation". Interpolation explains it for one independent variable; manifold-boundary reduction, continuum limits and the renormalization group are read as its instances; the review ends with consequences from systems biology to autoencoders. | Read |
| [NOTE-2247](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2247.md) | Transtrum, Machta & Sethna 2011 — the geometry of nonlinear least squares: widths, boundaries and curvature of sloppy model manifolds | The long treatment: a sloppy model's manifold is a bounded hyper-ribbon whose widths fall by a roughly constant factor, argued from polynomial interpolation; in natural or log units, from a central point, the geodesic widths match the Jacobian's singular values (≈ √λ) for a sum of exponentials and a 4-4-2 tanh network, but not in magnitude for PC12. Boundaries are where the metric JᵀJ is singular, usually at parameters 0 or ∞, also on finite fold lines (equal rates); with fewer data than twice the parameters, finite singular points are generic. Fitting fails at boundaries; geodesic acceleration and delayed gratification help. | Read |
| [NOTE-2252](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2252.md) | Gutenkunst, Waterfall, Casey, Brown, Myers & Sethna 2007 — sloppy spectra across seventeen systems-biology models | Seventeen ODE models from the systems-biology literature, 9 to 234 parameters each: the Hessian of a least-squares deviation of all time courses, in log parameters at the published values, has eigenvalues that "span many decades", "approximately evenly spaced in their logarithm", with "no well-defined cutoff", along eigenvectors skewed from the bare parameter axes. Read as the Fisher information of an idealized fit, it leaves many parameters more than 100% uncertain; in one model a collective fit constrains a prediction that direct measurement would match only with all 24 relevant parameters known to ±25%. | [NOTE-2253](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2253.md) | Transtrum & Qiu 2014 — model reduction by manifold boundaries | The manifold boundary approximation method (MBAM): a sloppy model's manifold is "bounded with a hierarchy of widths"; follow a geodesic from the fitted point along the Fisher metric's least sensitive direction until the smallest eigenvalue "approaches zero" at a boundary, identify the boundary with a limit in the model's equations and evaluate it, refit, and repeat. The EGFR model goes from 48 parameters to 12, a generalized Ising chain to one block-spin step. The method needs a hierarchy of edges and corners, not only of widths: an ellipsoid has the widths and "no corners". | Read |
| [NOTE-2256](../../../record/notes.d/NOTE-2256.md) | Quinn, Abbott, Transtrum, Machta & Sethna — Information geometry for multiparameter models: New perspectives on the origin of simplicity | A review of the Sethna-group programme. Many multiparameter models have Fisher eigenvalues and model-manifold widths that are hierarchical, roughly equally spaced in log over several decades: sloppy models, hyperribbon manifolds. The ubiquity is "an empirical fact", bounded rigorously only for least-squares models smooth in their control variable; a hyperribbon gives a low-dimensional description only where many widths fall below the precision demanded; and the explanations for hyperribbons in renormalizable physics and in least-squares fitting "seem completely different". | Read |
